integrationReview.reason: README.md and .env.example document AUTH_SERVICE_URL with a POST /auth/validate default contract, enforced on all sensitive process and outbox mutation endpoints (fail-closed).
integrationReview.contract: Bearer-token identity validation via POST /auth/validate (path/method configurable)
integrationReview.failureMode: Mutation endpoints fail closed (reject) when auth-microservice is unreachable or validation fails; GET /health remains public and unaffected.
integrationReview.validation: Focused auth contract tests (per TASKS.md 2026-08-30 review fixes) and verify:deployment-wiring.

integrationReview.reason: .env.example documents BPCP_DATABASE_URL as required, with README.md stating the service refuses to start without it; process registry, audit history, event outbox, and workflow instances are TypeORM-persisted.
integrationReview.contract: TypeORM entities and migrations for process registry, audit history, event outbox, and workflow instances
integrationReview.failureMode: The service refuses to start without a configured database connection; there is no degraded in-memory fallback for persisted entities.
integrationReview.validation: verify:process-registry and verify:instances verification scripts; npm test.

integrationReview.reason: No Redis client, environment variable, or documented usage exists anywhere in this repository.

integrationReview.contract: Structured log delivery per the platform logging contract
integrationReview.failureMode: Logging outage degrades observability without blocking mutation or query endpoints.

integrationReview.reason: BPCP explicitly does not own notification delivery channels (AGENTS.md, README.md Boundaries). notifications-microservice is registered only as a known service capability (e.g. template-ref-delivery) in BPCP's capability/workflow registries for workflow definitions to reference, not called directly by BPCP itself.
No AI-microservice integration is documented or referenced anywhere in this repository's code, .env.example, or docs.
BPCP explicitly does not own monetary finality or payment capture (README.md Boundaries, AGENTS.md Intent).
BPCP explicitly does not own product catalog data (AGENTS.md Intent, README.md Boundaries).
BPCP coordinates process/workflow lifecycle, not order processing; no orders-microservice integration is documented or referenced.
BPCP has no physical inventory or warehouse concern.
BPCP explicitly does not own invoice legal totals (README.md Boundaries); it does not integrate with invoices-microservice directly.
No object-storage usage was found in this repository's code, .env.example, or docs.

README.md, .env.example, and AGENTS.md document an approved RabbitMQ topic transport adapter for process events (exchange bpcp.events, routing prefix bpcp.process), currently env-gated by BPCP_EVENT_BUS_ENABLED and off by default.
integrationReview.contract: Durable process event outbox dispatched over a RabbitMQ topic transport adapter when enabled
integrationReview.failureMode: When the event bus is disabled or unreachable, events remain durably queued in the PostgreSQL-backed outbox for later bounded dispatch/replay rather than being lost.

integrationReview.reason: This runtime service must remain discoverable through the ecosystem documentation index, consistent with every other runtime-service repository's adoption profile.
integrationReview.contract: Direct Git repository ingestion and repository-scoped retrieval
integrationReview.configuration: Tracked in the canonical repository registry and docs-RAG index
integrationReview.failureMode: When docs-RAG is unavailable, Git remains authoritative.
integrationReview.validation: Repository documents resolve to the owning repository path and remain discoverable.

integrationReview.reason: .env.example documents MONITORING_SERVICE_URL, and runtime health/rollout readiness must be observable through the shared monitoring stack.
integrationReview.contract: GET /health and Kubernetes readiness checks for rollout control
integrationReview.configuration: MONITORING_SERVICE_URL and deployment probes in k8s manifests
integrationReview.failureMode: An unhealthy service is prevented from passing rollout readiness and is reported to the owner.
integrationReview.validation: The monitoring stack confirms health, readiness, and service availability.

integrationReview.reason: The service persists process registry, audit history, event outbox, and workflow instance data durably in PostgreSQL via BPCP_DATABASE_URL, which requires backup coverage consistent with other ecosystem databases.
integrationReview.contract: Scheduled/manual PostgreSQL backups for the BPCP database
integrationReview.configuration: backup-db.sh or equivalent invoked against the BPCP PostgreSQL database
integrationReview.failureMode: Missed backups increase data-loss risk on failure; this must be flagged as an operational blocker if backup automation lapses.
integrationReview.validation: Backup script execution and restore-drill evidence.
